text: A jury in a criminal trial consists of twelve ordinary citizens who reflect a cross-section of society.
Describe the selection process for the jury. Assess the extent to which the statement above is
true. [25]
Eva thinks that she has been unfairly dismissed from her job. She wishes to take her case to a
tribunal.
Explain how tribunals work and discuss the advantages and disadvantages of using a tribunal for
this type of dispute. [25]
Describe the legislative process in Parliament. To what extent is this an effective form of
law-making? [25]
Explain the powers of the police to stop and search a suspect in a public place.
Assess whether these powers adequately balance the rights of an individual against the need to
investigate crime. [25]
Describe the role and recruitment of judges. Assess whether the judiciary is drawn from too narrow
a section of society. [25]
The use of delegated legislation allows too much law to be made by unelected representatives.
Explain the types of delegated legislation and assess the extent to which the statement above is
true. [25]
